title: Interop: cross-check mimi-content vectors with phnx-im/mimi-content (Air)
description: Run mimid's content fixtures (moving to -10, see mimid-1wgh.2.26) through phnx-im/mimi-content and vice versa, both decode and encode. That crate is used in production by Phoenix's Air app, so a mismatch is a real-app interop bug. Note phnx mimi-content is still at -08/-09 (Konrad's PR #20 to -09 open); differences from -10 changes are expected, not bugs. Repo has no license file: Mark decides whether/how to contribute a -10 update.
design:
PLAN (2026-11-02, awaiting Mark). phnx-im/mimi-content: main 31487f9 (2026-10-19, pre-09; Air's crate) and PR #20 head 6378938 (kkohbrok, 'update to draft-ietf-mimi-content-09', open). License correction: the repo is REUSE-licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later (Cargo.toml license field, LICENSES/AGPL-3.0-or-later.txt, REUSE.toml; docs CC-BY-4.0); GitHub shows none only because there is no top-level LICENSE file. API: MimiContent::deserialize/serialize, message_id(sender, room).
A. Phoenix decodes mimid's oracle: a standalone harness at tools/interop/phoenix (own [workspace], mimi_content as a git dependency pinned by rev; README tells how to switch between main and PR #20) runs every WG -10 example in crates/mimi-content/tests/fixtures/wg-10 through Phoenix: deserialize, serialize, require byte-identical output, and compute the message ID with the sender/room URIs mimid's tests use (copied with a pointer to tests/common/mod.rs). Run against both revs; results to beads, not files.
B. mimid decodes Phoenix's output: the harness writes Phoenix-encoded messages built from fixed inputs through Phoenix's API (simple_markdown_message with a fixed salt, simple_receipt, a message with senderUri/roomUri and unknown extensions, a multipart, an external part) into crates/mimi-content/tests/fixtures/phoenix with PROVENANCE (repo, rev, SHA-256, license AGPL-3.0-or-later per REUSE, generator command); a new crates/mimi-content/tests/phoenix_fixtures.rs decodes each, compares with the generator's inputs, re-encodes and requires identical bytes.
Every mismatch is judged against draft-ietf-mimi-content-10 (and -09 for PR #20): differences that come from Phoenix being pre-09/-09 (e.g. 4096-byte extension cap, tagged URLs) are recorded as expected, not bugs; real Phoenix bugs become beads labelled upstream ('phoenix: ...'); a mimid bug becomes a bug bead. Nothing is posted upstream without Mark's OK.
